final_candidates.decision_summary: Replacing a buried tryptophan with charged aspartate likely introduces a buried charge and packing defect, strongly destabilizing PsaE folding.
Phenylalanine in a predicted hydrophobic cluster replaced by aspartate should severely disrupt core packing and bury an uncompensated charge.
Phenylalanine-to-aspartate at an aromatic/hydrophobic position likely creates charge burial and loss of stabilizing packing.

stop_reason.detail: Further self-iteration is unlikely to improve the Top-3 without structural data or external evidence.

history.rationale: Removes a large hydrophobic tryptophan likely buried in the core, creating a cavity and disrupting packing.
Removing the large tryptophan side chain creates a core cavity, though glycine may be less destabilizing than a charged substitution.
Replaces a buried hydrophobic tryptophan with a charged aspartate, causing severe electrostatic and solvation incompatibility.
Buried tryptophan replaced by charged aspartate should severely disrupt the hydrophobic core and cost substantial folding energy.
Introduces a charged residue in place of an aromatic hydrophobic residue, likely disrupting core packing and stability.
Tyrosine is probably part of the hydrophobic/aromatic core; aspartate substitution should disrupt packing and introduce buried charge.
Charged substitution at a buried phenylalanine is expected to destabilize the hydrophobic interior.
Phenylalanine in a hydrophobic cluster replaced by a buried charged residue is highly destabilizing.
Phenylalanine to aspartate places a charged side chain in a likely hydrophobic environment, impairing folding.
Aromatic core position replaced by aspartate likely causes strong charge burial and packing defects.
Glycine substitution at a proline may increase backbone flexibility and remove a structurally constrained turn or kink.
Proline-to-glycine may increase backbone flexibility, but the effect is less certain and weaker than core-charge substitutions.

rejection.reason: Proline-to-glycine may increase backbone flexibility, but the effect is less certain and weaker than core-charge substitutions.

history.rationale: Introducing a bulky valine at a conserved glycine position may sterically clash and destabilize local backbone conformation.
Valine at a glycine position may cause steric strain, but confidence is lower and it is less directly tied to core disruption.

rejection.reason: Valine at a glycine position may cause steric strain, but confidence is lower and it is less directly tied to core disruption.

history.rationale: Charged aspartate at a buried valine likely disrupts hydrophobic core packing and folding stability.
Hydrophobic valine to charged aspartate should disrupt local packing and stability.
Large charged arginine replacing a buried leucine likely creates steric and electrostatic destabilization.
Leucine to charged arginine is destabilizing, but arginine may snorkel and is less reliably disruptive than buried aspartate.
Isoleucine to aspartate inserts a charged residue into a hydrophobic region, likely disrupting the folded state.
Isoleucine in a hydrophobic segment replaced by aspartate likely perturbs the core, though neighboring polar backbone may partly compensate.
Buried isoleucine in the hydrophobic segment 32-40 replaced by aspartate should add a strong buried charge and disrupt packing.
Valine in the same hydrophobic cluster replaced by aspartate likely causes severe charge burial and loss of core packing.
